newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro Commission sets course for larger EU future.
newsitem.headline: Euro Commission sets course for larger EU future.

text.p: The European Commission on Wednesday set the course for the European Union into the next century, officially unveiling plans to embrace five members of the former Communist bloc.
Publishing what it has dubbed Agenda 2000, the Commission said Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Estonia and Slovenia should be invited to begin EU membership talks along with Cyprus next year.

It also called for a reform of the EU's Common Agricultural Policy and its support programmes for the bloc's poorer nations and regions to allow for the enlargement into the economically emerging east.
"We have an historic opportunity, carrying with it profound changes," European Commission President Jacques Santer told the European Parliament.

Documents prepared by the Commission to judge the readiness of 10 eastern European countries for membership also said that although Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia, Bulgaria and Romania had not made the grade, they should be kept in what amounts to a waiting room where they can prepare for membership at their own pace.
The Commission laid down a list of policy challenges faced by the EU to prepare for its new members.

They include a radical reform of the Common Agricultural Policy including dairy, cereals and beef intervention price cuts of 10, 20 and 30 percent respectively, to be partially compensated by direct income payments.
It said a new intergovernmental conference of EU member states would be needed to loosen up the EU's decision-making procedures for the day it has new members.

The Commission also said the EU should continue to limit its self-financing at a rate of 1.27 percent of Gross Domestic Product, relying on ecomomic growth to provide the extra funds needed in th immediate future.
